name: Adaiah
overview: Adaiah was a male priest from the tribe of Levi who lived in Jerusalem. He is specifically identified as the son of Jeroham. His priestly role and Levitical heritage place him within the God-ordained system of worship and temple service during the post-exilic period.
namesAndTitles: The name Adaiah means 'adornment of YHWH,' reflecting a connection to the LORD. This proper name, recorded in Nehemiah 11:12, underscores the honor and reverence associated with his identity as a servant of God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records that Adaiah was the son of Jeroham, establishing his lineage within a priestly family. No other family relationships are noted beyond this direct filial connection.
scriptureSignificance: Adaiah's significance lies in his role as a priest from the tribe of Levi residing in Jerusalem after the exile, contributing to the restoration and continuation of temple worship. His mention in Nehemiah highlights the reestablishment of God's covenant community and the faithful service of priests in the renewed city. Through his priestly service, Adaiah represents the preservation of God's ordinances and the spiritual heritage of Israel.
